question: Following an investigation by The Observer, Lighthouse Reports, Le Monde and Der Spiegel, videos have been released showing French security forces trying to destabilise small boats carrying migrants in the English Channel in an attempt to stop them reaching the UK coast.

It is clear that French authorities are using aggressive tactics: circling boats causing waves to flood them, ramming into boats while threatening migrants with pepper spray and puncturing boats when they are already at sea, forcing people to swim back to shore.

Although the French authorities have previously refused the UK’s requests – and money – to intercept boats at sea, evidence shows that such practices are on the rise. Given that these ‘pushback’ actions are relatively common: 1.
What measures are being taken to investigate the events that have come to light?
What does the Commission intend to do with regard to the French authorities to stop the loss of human lives in such circumstances and enforce international law?
answer: 1. The safe and effective management of the external borders of the EU must always be firmly rooted in the respect for EU and international law, including fundamental rights as enshrined in the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights.

It is the obligation of every Member State, including France, to investigate any alleged violation of the law perpetrated by its national authorities, to establish the facts and ensure there are appropriate consequences for any identified wrongdoing.

The Commission understands that a complaint has been lodged with the French human rights ombudsman and that an investigation is ongoing, and expects the investigation to be conducted swiftly, thoroughly and transparently. 2. Search and rescue operations at sea fall under international maritime law, and its implementation is a matter of national competence.

The Commission does not have the powers to enforce international law. It is the responsibility of each Member State to appropriately implement and respect the applicable EU and international law, and to investigate and prosecute any identified failure to do so.
This therefore applies to all activities performed to manage the external borders of the EU, including its maritime borders, where the EU’s border management acquis must be applied in full.

This includes inter alia the respect for all fundamental rights obligations, as well as the correct implementation of the non-refoulement principle, and ensuring that all actions ‘compl[y] with the principles of necessity, proportionality, and precaution’ (1). The Commission will follow the developments and measures taken closely.
Regulation 2019/1896 on the European Border and Coast Guard, Annex V(1).
